title: Observed Upper Savannah hydrology and Eighteenmile scientific context
edition: 2026-10-13 observed flow, original basin geography and source quality
sections: Observed Eighteenmile Creek and Lake Hartwell conditions

The 2023 lake-arm study and the original agency measurements provide a dated receiving-water context for the watershed scenarios. This edition retains the recovered 75 selected chlorophyll-a results at five sites, all 920 recovered water-quality result rows, 2,192 daily mean flows at USGS 02186702 during 2020–2025, and the 2023 reported discharge quantities used below. Sampling covered 5 April–17 October 2023. Concentrations, daily flows, dated discharge quantities and annual watershed exports retain their original units and temporal support.

The strongest chlorophyll response occurs within the lake arm. The published surface means for total phosphorus decrease from 0.08 mg/L at SV-268 to 0.01 mg/L at open-lake SV-840, while published total nitrogen means decrease from 1.00 to 0.22 mg/L. Chlorophyll-a instead peaks in the seasonal mean at SV-838. This spatial pattern gives the scenario analysis two distinct features to address: nutrient delivery from the tributary and biological response within the receiving lake.

sections: SV-838 is the highest station on 12 of the 15 shared visits and exceeds SV-840 on all 15 paired sampling dates, by 6.77–30.51 ug/L; its mean is 3.97 times the SV-840 mean. The maxima occur on different dates among sites, from early May to mid-October. The observations support a persistent site contrast and substantial seasonal variation. Specific nutrient limitation, travel time and lake retention require their own model terms and measurements.
Flow during the monitoring campaign

USGS 02186702 provides a complete 365-day approved daily-mean record for 2023: mean discharge 68.42 ft3/s and total observed volume 61.100 million m3. The 196-day lake-study window averages 63.52 ft3/s. Across the 15 chlorophyll sampling dates, daily means average 49.11 ft3/s and range from 21.1 to 96.2 ft3/s; none reaches the annual 95th percentile of 134.8 ft3/s.

Four sampling visits follow a flow at or above that annual 95th percentile within the previous seven days. The prior window excludes the sampling day, retains the actual daily record and keeps the original agency qualifiers. These cases provide observed event timing for interpreting the lake samples.

Runoff uses the original gauge drainage area of 48.6 square miles. Estimated is an additional qualifier; it may overlap approval status.

Reported source quantities and their position relative to the gauge

The original stream-network route places Milliken, Pickens Upper and Pickens Middle upstream of USGS 02186702. Pendleton-Clemson lies on the same indexed reach downstream of the gauge. Membership in the gauge's whole catchment alone does not distinguish the two ends of that reach; the source NHD measures and upstream network membership provide the required direction.

Reported daily rates are multiplied by their actual monitoring-period calendar days. Where a reporting period crosses a month boundary, its reported average rate is applied to each overlapping day; the original period, rate, selected DMR value identifiers and quantification status remain attached to the monthly rows.
Monthly source quantities in observed flow

The upstream reported-volume ratio increases as gauge flow declines: 2.30% in January and 11.94% in October. This supplies a time-resolved source context beyond the 4.24% annual ratio. The gross phosphorus mass divided by observed gauge volume ranges from 0.00466 mg/L in April to 0.04975 mg/L in November. This index expresses the reported source mass at the gauge's observed dilution volume; a receiving-water concentration calculation additionally requires delivery, retention, travel time and other sources.

Nitrogen species and reporting cohorts remain separate. A blank annual complete-cohort quantity retains missing coverage rather than converting it to zero.

sections: Use in the scenario interpretation

Read the land-cover alternatives as changes in annual diffuse nutrient and sediment delivery over their modeled catchments. Carry dated point-source quantities through their own spatial route, then interpret the receiving lake against the actual seasonal observations. This structure allows conservation changes to be evaluated alongside observed source pressure, hydrologic variability and the lake-arm response.

The 15-date chlorophyll record samples moderate daily flows while retaining four visits after larger preceding events. It supports station and seasonal comparisons; an annual receiving-water load requires concentration sampling across the relevant flow distribution. The two original routine-clock overlaps are resolved by the retained study calendar and local-clock reconciliation, with both competing source activities preserved. The measured cohort has 15 selected results at each station; the separately transcribed printed Table 7 counts of four for SV-374 and SV-840 remain in the source notes.

All 920 recovered water-quality results retain their quantitation class: 676 numeric results, 240 below a reporting threshold and four above a reporting threshold. The figures below use the selected quantified chlorophyll activities. Bounds and original reported values remain available for the broader measured-water-quality desk.

Sources: South Carolina's Lake Hartwell–Eighteenmile Creek Lake Arm 2023 Nutrient Study, Technical Report 010-2023; original SCDES WQX activities recovered through the Water Quality Portal; USGS daily-mean discharge parameter 00060, statistic 00003, method 126695; original EPA DMR reporting periods; original SCDES outfall geometry and USGS NLDI flowline indexing. Source URLs, retrieval metadata, selected identifiers and full numerical precision travel with the retained files.
Regional daily-flow source explorer

The linked source explorer carries all 59,701 original daily records at 29 gauges during 2020–2025: 59,700 numeric flows and one original nonnumeric agency value. It retains original qualifiers, JSON response positions and RDB text-line positions. The 174 gauge-year periods include 149 complete numeric calendar years, of which 144 are fully approved. Source-specific reference years, gaps, estimated/provisional records and actual Eighteenmile study dates remain visible.

Use each gauge's measured discharge and source drainage-area metadata with its own catchment. Discharge timing, volume and runoff depth support hydrologic context; matching native nutrient or sediment exports requires concentration or load observations at the same outlet and temporal support. The retained lake measurements and separately routed reported point-source quantities keep their existing units, dates, coverage and constituent identities.

sections: Routine nutrient observations: original visits and censor bounds

This section uses the original 2023 SWS-2023 routine nutrient cohort at SV-268 and SV-374: 96 reported results in 24 source activities, with 12 visits at each station. Twenty-four total-nitrogen values combine Kjeldahl nitrogen and nitrate plus nitrite within the same source activity, date, fraction, project and sample clock. Ammonia remains part of Kjeldahl nitrogen and is not added again. The 120 calculated value rows comprise those 96 original results and 24 within-activity sums.

Each reported below-limit result retains a conservative nonnegative concentration enclosure and its original strict relation. Mean lower and upper endpoints use every selected visit and the same denominator; no half-limit value or zero-valued measurement is substituted. These enclosures describe retained measurement limits, rather than statistical confidence intervals.

sections.caption: All original routine visits; the station date sets differ. Full-precision values, activity identities and original source rows accompany the report.

sections: The routine nutrient cohort and the separate special-study chlorophyll campaign retain their own dates, depths and programme identities. Their counts are presented separately throughout the source tables.
Routine nutrient contrasts within observed flow bands

The complete 365-day approved record at upstream gauge USGS 02186702 defines discharge quartile boundaries of 30.6, 53.9 and 75.3 ft³/s. Q1 includes values at or below the first boundary; Q2 and Q3 exclude their lower boundary and include their upper boundary; Q4 contains values above 75.3 ft³/s. Each original routine visit is assigned its same-calendar-day gauge mean.

sections.caption: Descriptive, unmatched visit groups with two to five visits per station/band. Flow bands retain the actual gauge-day context; they do not establish matching water parcels or hydraulic travel time.

sections: The phosphorus and within-activity total-nitrogen mean enclosures remain separated between these stations in all four observed-flow bands. Interpreting transport, retention or annual nutrient load requires the relevant outlet geometry, concentration coverage and flow-weighting method.
Same-date routine measurements and the June 12 event

May 17 is the sole calendar date shared by the two routine station cohorts. The original SV-268 activity began 13:39 EDT and SV-374 began 11:32 EDT; the upstream gauge daily mean was 64.7 ft³/s. The table retains this timing difference.

sections.caption: 2023-05-17 source activities AF02075 and AF02069; full original activity prefixes and source-result IDs are retained in same_date.csv.

sections: The June 12 SV-268 activity AF03778 coincided with a 604 ft³/s gauge daily mean, at the 99.315th midrank percentile of the year's daily values. Its constituent contrasts are calculated against the other 11 routine visits at that station, all below the annual gauge 95th percentile.

sections.caption: Constituents respond differently: event phosphorus was 0.180 mg/L, while within-activity total nitrogen was 0.660 mg/L. Comparison dates, source activities and original strict bounds travel with june12_contrast.csv.

sections: Routine nutrient source files
Paired chlorophyll and microcystin observations

The retained paired analysis compares 75 selected chlorophyll observations across five stations and 15 dates, yielding 150 same-date station contrasts. The complete microcystin campaign contains 85 original results. Exact station, date, displayed-clock and timezone matching links 67 records to the selected chlorophyll cohort; these linked records support 128 spatial microcystin contrasts. Both unmatched clocks and missing same-date activities remain visible in the source report.

SV-840 had lower chlorophyll than SV-838 on all 15 shared dates; the mean SV-840 minus SV-838 difference was −18.032 µg/L. Their linked microcystin values were higher at SV-840 on seven dates, lower on five, and unresolved by reporting limits on one. Chlorophyll and microcystin therefore retain separate reported responses in this source analysis.

The published agency protocol describes surface sampling at 0.3 m for microcystin alongside chlorophyll. Individual WQP microcystin activity depth fields are blank, while selected chlorophyll activities encode 0.3 m. The report preserves both sources and every original activity identity.

sections: Original gauge and contributing-basin geography

The flow explorer links 14 original NLDI whole-catchment polygons to their gauges in the 29-station observed flow record. The offline report retains all 29,049 original polygon vertices, original NLDI point coordinates, reach codes and flowline measures. Selecting a basin or point opens the corresponding hydrograph and its original daily records. The display uses Web Mercator while retaining the original longitude/latitude geometry.

Original coordinates were evaluated for all 169 point/catchment pairs among the 13 added gauges. Forty-eight pairs place the original point inside the published whole catchment. The Eighteenmile gauge is also inside its original whole catchment. Original NWIS coordinates and their NAD83 datum remain separate from the NLDI geographic coordinates.
